title: Break up the 205-line status function in status.rs
summary: Refactor `Athena::status` (crates/athena-core/src/status.rs, line 2079, ~205 lines) into private helper methods or functions so every function is at most 200 lines. Behavior and output stay identical. The audience is code health, which measures the limit, and the maintainers who read the file.

defaults_applied.how: cargo test, clippy and fmt must pass.
Break up the long function along real responsibilities instead of trimming lines to land just under 200.
Existing tests are run to show behavior is unchanged.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/status.rs. `status()` (lines 2079-2346) loads Records and the RecordSet, then builds job lines (jobs_by_state, recent, open, first_round), intervention counts, per-class forecast headlines, the pending quantities, the bootstrap note and the `next` action lines. It ends by assembling StatusView. The `trace` method follows it and is untouched.

Natural seams in `status()`: (1) the job loop that produces jobs_by_state, recent, open and first_round; (2) the per-class forecast headlines; (3) the pending-quantity resolution join; (4) the bootstrap note; (5) the `next` line construction. Extract these into private free functions or methods that take `&Records` or `&[JobLine]`. Keep the order of `next` pushes exactly as it is.

The file is 916 production lines, well under the 2000 line limit. Only the 200 line per-function limit is breached. Whole-file splitting into modules is not needed. The big test module stays where it is.
No record or data files are added, so the records allow-list and round-trip tests are not affected. No rule is added or tightened, so no refusal-rate criterion applies.
Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, lint config) are not needed. Do not add lint allows to silence the limit.

acceptance_criteria.text: In crates/athena-core/src/status.rs, no function, including the `status` method, is longer than 200 lines. A reader can check this by reading the file. `status` is now clearly shorter than 205 lines and delegates to named helpers.
The diff touches only crates/athena-core/src/status.rs. The StatusView fields, public signatures and `next` line texts and order are unchanged, and no existing test is edited or deleted.
`cargo test -p athena-core` passes with the existing status tests unchanged.
`cargo clippy --all-targets` reports no warnings, and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
The extracted helpers have doc comments written for an outside reader, and no lint suppression is added to hide the length.

out_of_scope: Changing the `trace` method or any other function
Changing the status output, next-step text or StatusView shape
departures: A mechanical single-file refactor with a clear seam is somewhat more likely to pass than the reference. The file is large, so cold builds add time.
